slices.focus: Company maintenance triggers an apartment move to a smaller, quieter unit near the terminal, forcing Ayaka to confront how much work paperwork had colonized her home.
slices.summary: Company building maintenance forces Ayaka to move. She chooses a smaller, quieter unit near Hakata terminal over a larger one farther away, prioritizing commute reliability and sleep quality. Sorting years of accumulated terminal paperwork (old timetables, handwritten notes, operational folders) becomes an unexpectedly emotional process of deciding what deserves space in her home. She adopts a one-tray rule for incoming papers and sets a weekend cycling deadline.
open_loops: Moving costs and setup expenses tighten an already-lean budget
The one-tray rule may collapse during storm season when paperwork surges
Books still unpacked — the apartment still feels provisional
